Acute Myeloid Leukemia involves malignant transformation of myeloid progenitor cells.  
Myeloid progenitors normally give rise to granulocytes, monocytes, erythrocytes, and megakaryocytes (which produce platelets).  
NK cells and T cells arise from lymphoid progenitors, not myeloid progenitors.  
Platelets are derived from megakaryocytes, which come from the myeloid lineage.  

Final answer: (B)
